prompt_context_by_prefix.ip:
Use these preferred technical term translations when relevant:
- flow (Q): дебит
- velocity (v): скорост
- head loss (h_L): загуба на напор
- emitter: капкоотделител
- distribution uniformity (DU): равномерност на разпределение
- low-quarter distribution uniformity (DU_lq): равномерност на разпределение по долната четвърт
- application rate (PR): норма на поливане
- lateral: латерал
- mainline: главен тръбопровод
- reach: участък
- velocity head (H_v): скоростен напор
- friction loss (h_f): загуби от триене
- minor loss (h_m): местни загуби
- energy grade line (EGL): енергийна линия
- upstream: нагоре по течението
- downstream: надолу по течението

ip.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
ip.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg OPEN QUESTION (2026-07): native engineer corrected 'дебит' to 'водно количество' in hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings (rc_, or_). Whether to replace 'дебит' suite-wide (incl. pipes/irrigation) is pending their clarification; keep 'дебит' elsewhere until answered. ENGINEER CLARIFICATION (2026-07-06): 'дебит is a typical colloquial call of the word — regular people and non-hydraulic engineers use it. In university (hydraulic engineering) they used водно количество for Q, never дебит. I guess both work.' So both are acceptable; водно количество is the academic/hydraulic-engineering register, дебит the general register. Still an open decision whether to standardize on водно количество suite-wide.

ip.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
ip.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

ip.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.
ip.translation_notes: 'Head' in the hydraulic sense (energy per unit weight) does not translate literally in many languages — use the established civil/hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'gubitak pritiska' (= pressure loss), which is technically the same concept expressed in pressure terms rather than head terms. The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-09 (category-3 wave-1 sprint): ro/tr/id translations were pressure-loss-sense ('pierdere de presiune'/'basınç kaybı'/'kehilangan tekanan'), contradicting this note's own guidance. Independently flagged by both the ro and tr wave-1 translation agents; corrected to head-loss-sense ('pierdere de sarcină'/'yük kaybı'/'kehilangan tinggi tekan') to match what both agents actually used in lib/lang.ec.ro.php and lib/lang.ec.tr.php. de's 'Druckverlust' was left as-is (not flagged; German engineering practice uses pressure/head loss terms more interchangeably in pipe-flow context) but is worth a second look in a future audit. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-09 (category-3 fa sprint): fa was 'افت فشار' (literally 'pressure loss', same pressure-loss-sense defect class as the ro/tr/id fix above), while the fa file's own mphl_ head-loss labels already used 'افت هد' (head loss) and 'هد' is an established loanword elsewhere in the file (هد سرعت = velocity head). Standardized to 'افت هد' suite-wide for fa and fixed dw_/hw_ labels in lib/lang.ec.fa.php to match. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-10 (category-3 sw wave-3 sprint): glossary sw value was 'upotevu wa shinikizo' (= pressure loss), the same pressure-loss-sense defect class as the ro/tr/id/fa fixes above. But lib/lang.ec.sw.php's own dw_main_desc/dw_main_menu/dw_main_title/mphl_main_desc/mphl_main_menu/mphl_main_title (and mpf_velocity_head, ws_headWaterHeight, or_head, mhp_gross_head elsewhere in the file) all already establish 'Kichwa' (head) as the suite's real Swahili word for hydraulic head, not 'shinikizo' (pressure). Standardized the glossary to 'upotevu wa kichwa' to match the file's own established, correct usage instead of the stale pressure-sense glossary value. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-10 (category-3 ps wave-3 sprint): glossary ps value was 'د سر زیان' (زیان = damage/loss), but lib/lang.ec.ps.php's own dw_/hw_/mpf_/mphl_ head-loss labels (40+ occurrences suite-wide) all already use ضیاع, not زیان, for 'loss' (e.g. existing dw_main_menu 'Darcy-Weisbach د پایپ سر ضیاع', mphl_total_loss). زیان does not occur anywhere in the file. Standardized the glossary to 'د سر ضیاع' to match the file's actual established usage, same defect class as the sw fix above.

ip.context: A drip irrigation emitter (dripper/micro-sprinkler) that delivers water at a controlled low flow rate directly to the soil or plant root zone. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: Use the field term most familiar to irrigation practitioners in the target language. Arabic: 'قطارة' (dripper) is the field term, preferred over the academic 'مُصدِر'. Spanish: 'gotero' is field-common in Latin America alongside the technical 'emisor'. Ukrainian: 'крапельниця' is the field term used by irrigation workers. zh CORRECTED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 QA): the wave-2 zh translating agent initially deviated to the generic academic term '灌水器' throughout ip_ keys, reasoning that the calculator's emitter-exponent model (x from ~0 to 0.5) is generic rather than drip-only. Reverted to the established glossary field term '滴头' (dripper) for suite-wide consistency with the ar/es/uk pattern above — this glossary's own policy is field-term-over-academic-generality across all languages, and a generic hydraulic model doesn't change what practitioners actually call the part.

ip.context: Ratio of minimum to average emitter flow rate in a drip or sprinkler system. DU = q_min / q_avg. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: Use the irrigation engineering standard term. 'Uniformity' refers to how evenly water is distributed across the field, not physical evenness of the system. When the source says 'low-quarter DU', see the separate 'low-quarter distribution uniformity' entry. Hebrew: אחידות — never the nonword הוודות (found in shipped he file).

ip.context: Irrigation statistic: average of the lowest quarter of measured emitter flows divided by the overall average. Referenced in Irrigation Pressure notes as "textbook low-quarter Distribution Uniformity".
ip.translation_notes: Use the established irrigation-engineering phrase; do not invent one. "Textbook" is an adjective meaning "as defined in standard textbooks" — fr rendered it "manuel" (manual check), wrong. he: uniformity = אחידות, never the nonword הוודות. Wave-1 coinages (2026-07, category-4 sprint): fr="uniformité de distribution du quart inférieur", ro="Uniformitatea Distribuției de sfert inferior", ru="равномерность распределения по нижней четверти", uk="рівномірність розподілу по низькій чверті", bg="равномерност на разпределение по долната четвърт", sr="равномерност расподеле нижег квартила", hr="jednolikost distribucije niske grupe", cs="Uniformita distribuce nízké čtvrtiny", tr="düşük-çeyrek Dağıtım Uniformluğu", id="Keseragaman Distribusi kuartal-bawah". es/pt/it/de already had glossary coverage pre-sprint. Not yet native-reviewed. ur ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 sprint): "نچلی چوتھائی تقسیم یکسانیت" (lower-quarter distribution uniformity) reuses the established ur terms چوتھائی (quarter), تقسیم (distribution), یکسانیت (uniformity, already glossary term for plain "distribution uniformity"). Not yet native-reviewed. hi ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'निम्न-चतुर्थांश वितरण एकरूपता' (low-quarter distribution uniformity) reuses the glossary's own hi="वितरण एकरूपता" for the base "distribution uniformity" term and prefixes "निम्न-चतुर्थांश" (low-quarter), matching the wave-1 pattern of naming the concept literally (fr/ru/uk/id etc.) rather than inventing a new metaphor. NOTE: the hi ip_ file's own pre-sprint text mistakenly used 'पाठ्यपुस्तक' (textbook) where the current English source says 'standard' — corrected to 'मानक' (standard) in lib/lang.ec.hi.php during this sprint; do not reintroduce पाठ्यपुस्तक. ar ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'انتظام التوزيع للربع الأدنى' (uniformity of distribution of the lowest quarter) reuses the glossary's own ar="انتظام التوزيع" base term for plain "distribution uniformity" (switched suite-wide in this sprint from a prior 'توحيد' root to 'انتظام', which better conveys 'evenness' rather than 'unification') and appends 'للربع الأدنى' (of the lowest quarter), naming the concept literally like the fr/ru/uk/id wave-1 coinages. Where the English source's own qualifier 'standard' appears in context (ip_du_estimate, ip_notes_3_def), it is rendered inline as 'القياسي' immediately after this base phrase, kept out of the pure glossary term here for parity with the other languages' entries. bn ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'নিম্ন-চতুর্থাংশ বিতরণ সমতা' (low-quarter distribution uniformity), built on the glossary's own bn="বিতরণ সমতা" base term, naming the concept literally. fa ADDED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 re-translation): 'یکنواختی توزیع ربع پایین' (low-quarter distribution uniformity), built on the glossary's own fa="یکنواختی توزیع" base term; where English says "standard" it is rendered inline as "استاندارد" immediately after this base phrase, same pattern as ar.
ip.preferred_translation: равномерност на разпределение по долната четвърт

ip.context: Depth of water applied per unit time by a drip or sprinkler system. PR = q / A_e. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: In irrigation, 'application rate' or 'precipitation rate' (for sprinklers) or 'irrigation rate'. Use the field irrigation term. Do not use a water-quality or chemical-application connotation.

ip.context: Irrigation branch line carrying emitters, fed by the mainline. Pairs with "mainline". Appears throughout Irrigation Pressure.
ip.translation_notes: Branch pipe of a drip/sprinkler system — NOT the adjective "side/lateral". Wrong renderings found: sw "taji" (crown). fr irrigation standard is "rampe". Keep one word per language and never alternate (it file mixed "laterale" and "manichetta").

ip.context: The trunk/supply pipe feeding the laterals in an irrigation system. Pairs with "lateral".
ip.translation_notes: Translate "main/mainline" as the trunk pipe, not the adjective "main". fr file left "main" untranslated ("Tronçons Main") — wrong.

ip.context: A segment of pipe or channel between two nodes/cross-sections. Table rows in Irrigation Pressure are reaches.
ip.translation_notes: Hydraulics noun, NOT "arrival/reaching" (ps "رسیدل" wrong), NOT "agent" (sw "mwakala" wrong), NOT "stripe" (km wrong). Bisection is the numerical root-finding method used to close the pressure loop in the Irrigation Pressure notes. (Wave 0, 2026-07-07, removed the former "right at the takeoff" and "draw off" wording from the English source.)

ip.context: Kinetic energy per unit weight, V²/2g — a height of water column.
ip.translation_notes: "Head" is a height of water column, never anatomical (cs "rychlostní hlava" wrong — use "rychlostní výška").

ip.context: Head loss along the pipe due to wall friction (Darcy-Weisbach). Symbol h_f (lowercase h reserved for loss components; capital H reserved for total/gross/net head, per label-normalization decision item 90, 2026-07-07). Manning Pipe Head Loss, Micro-Hydro Power, Irrigation Pressure table column.

Local head loss at fittings/valves/couplers (coefficient k_m). Canonical merged concept for the former 'junction loss' (mphl_) and 'minor loss' (mhp_/ip_). Manning Pipe Head Loss, Micro-Hydro Power, Irrigation Pressure.
ip.translation_notes: CANONICAL ENGLISH LABEL: "Minor (local) loss" (label-normalization decision, item 90, 2026-07-07). 'Minor ⇄ local' — a local/point loss at fittings, NOT a "smaller" loss; the '(local)' parenthetical fixes the mistranslation trap. Symbol h_m, coefficient k_m (lowercase h reserved for loss components; capital H reserved for total/gross/net head, per the same decision). am ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 am re-translation): 'ጥቃቅን (አካባቢያዊ) ኪሳራ' (tiqaqin (akababiyawi) kisara) mirrors the English structure word-for-word — 'ጥቃቅን' (minor/small) followed by the parenthetical '(አካባቢያዊ)' (local, i.e. of a specific place/area) — so the same mistranslation-blocking device English uses (the '(local)' qualifier preventing a 'smaller loss' misreading) is preserved in Amharic rather than silently dropped. Replaces the prior am file's 'የማያያዣ ኪሳራ' (connector/joint loss), which named the physical fitting rather than the local/point-loss concept. km ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 km re-translation): 'ការបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋាន' (local-basis loss) reuses មូលដ្ឋាន ('local', already established suite-wide for this exact merged concept in ip_km's tooltip 'មេគុណបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋានសរុប' = 'total local-loss coefficient'), so category-3 now converges on the same word ip_ already uses rather than coining a second competing term. Deliberately avoids 'តូច' (small), sidestepping the minor⇄smaller mistranslation trap the English '(local)' parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the km file's prior mphl_junction_loss value 'ការបាត់បង់ junction' (untranslated English word left in place). ps ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 ps wave-3 re-translation): 'ځایی ضیاع' (local loss) uses ځایی (local/positional) + the established ps loss word ضیاع, following the majority pattern already set by ar/fa/es/fr/hr/id/it/ro/ru/sr/tr/uk/ur/zh — all of which render this concept as 'local loss' alone rather than translating 'minor' literally, since the '(local)' qualifier is the operative disambiguator, not 'minor'. Deliberately avoids a word for 'small/minor' (e.g. کوچنی) to sidestep the same minor⇄smaller trap the English parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the prior ps file's 'د جنکشن ضیاع' (junction loss — the pre-consolidation, pre-item-90 term) and fixes its symbol from capital H_m to lowercase h_m.

ip.context: The total-head line (elevation + pressure head + velocity head) along a pipe or channel. Appears in Irrigation Pressure Method note.
ip.translation_notes: Use the established hydraulics term for the total-head line. NEVER calque word-by-word: es "Linea de Grado de Energia", fr "ligne d'energie grade", it "Linea di Grado Energia", ro "Linia Gradului Energetic", bg/uk "line of the energy class", cs "energy layer" are all wrong renderings found in shipped files.
Hydraulics direction, never software "upgrade" (my file error). tr: memba = upstream, mansap = downstream — a tr file flipped these; pin them.

ip.context: Direction away from the supply, toward the outlet / last emitter.
ip.translation_notes: Never software "downgrade". ar: downstream = المصب / أسفل المجرى (a file used المنبعية = source-side, wrong).
